slots.title: Fed meeting this week with rates on hold
slots.body:
The 10-year Treasury yield sat at 5.0% in the latest FMP snapshot (Oct. 23), with the gap between 2-year and 10-year yields at 0.31 percentage points.

Barron’s reported traders expect no change at this week’s Fed meeting after the September hike — the first increase since 2023.

Bloomberg’s weekend preview noted inflation still above target and that investors will parse the chair’s wording for how long a pause might last.

Prior U.S. session: $^GSPC −0.5% to 7,623.68; $^DJI −1.2% to 52,215.16.

What language from the Fed would you treat as the headline — inflation, growth, or something else?

slots.title: Brent crude down 2.0% as Iran stays in headlines
slots.body:
Brent crude: 114.33, −2.0% (−2.39 vs prior close 116.72).

WSJ reported Japanese stocks lower as Iran conflict and higher energy costs stayed in focus; chip and electronics names dragged the Nikkei.

Nikkei 225: 62,214.66, −0.8% (−478.5).

Reuters flagged oil concerns and the Fed meeting for Asian markets opening the week.

Hang Seng: 23,127.76, +0.1% — modest gain vs softer Japan.

Which cross-asset print are you watching first this week — oil, rates, or equities?

slots.title: Two regional Fed gauges land Monday
slots.body:
Monday’s U.S. data slate (medium impact on the FMP calendar):

Chicago Fed National Activity Index (Sep) — estimate −0.1; previous −0.04 (release window 12:30 ET).

Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index (Oct) — estimate 7; previous 9.8 (14:30 ET).

Both are broad reads on whether factory and overall activity is speeding up or slowing down — useful context ahead of the Fed’s rate decision later in the week.

VIX closed at 19.45, +2.2%, on the prior U.S. session.

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 25, 2026
slots.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished down 1.2%, a 652.82-point drop to 52,215.16, after trading between 52,055.10 and 52,696.70.
That was the heaviest index decline in the injected U.S. close set for the session.

The S&P 500 lost 0.5%, closing at 7,623.68 (−39.75 pts), with an intraday band of 7,612.07 to 7,660.15.
The Nasdaq Composite was comparatively steadier at −0.2%, ending at 25,955.34, while the Russell 2000 slipped 0.3% to 2,775.90.

The VIX rose 2.2% to 19.45, up from 19.03, with an intraday high of 20.66.
That move came alongside lower equity index closes rather than a calm, flat tape.

In commodities and FX proxies, gold futures (GCUSD) added 0.3% to $4,021.70.
The United States Oil Fund ($USO) rose 4.3% to $169.53, with a session high of $169.96 matching its 52-week high in the data.
Brent crude (BZUSD) was quoted down 2.0% at $114.33.
The dollar proxy UUP ticked up 0.2% to $28.96, and bitcoin (BTCUSD) was off 0.5% at $79,656.96.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-10-23) showed the 10-year at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.31 percentage points.
No new U.S. economic releases appeared in the session calendar block for Oct. 25.

Semiconductor-related megacaps split:
- $AMD +1.7%
- $TSM +1.5%

to $418.51, while $NVDA −0.6% to $210.96 and $AVGO −0.5% to $321.68.
$MSFT was up 0.7% to $524.51; $GOOGL −1.2% to $320.21.

Consumer and staples names were weak across the board in the mega-cap list: $KO −2.8% to $92.71, $PEP −2.2% to $135.77, $HD −2.4% to $319.83, and $WMT −1.0% to $119.89.
$COST −1.5% to $1,003.32.

$LLY −2.5% to $1,273.46 stood out among health megacaps.
$NFLX −1.8% to $65.85 closed near the lower end of its 52-week range (low $64.10 in the data).
$T −8.0% to $20.93 was the standout percentage move among active, widely recognized tickers in the session list.

Overseas indexes in the same payload were mixed to lower into the U.S. weekend: Nikkei 225 −0.8% to 62,214.66, FTSE 100 −0.3%, Hang Seng +0.1%, and the Germany proxy EWG −1.0%.

News flow in the feed pointed to the upcoming Federal Reserve rate decision and persistent oil-market attention ahead of Asian opens; those were narrative backdrops in headlines, not separate prints in the Oct. 25 U.S. close numbers.

Sector-level performance tags were empty in the injected sector block, so index and single-name moves above are the primary session map in the data.

slots.title: Tuesday: durable goods, home sales, confidence
slots.body:
Three U.S. releases land Tuesday, Oct. 27.

At 12:30 p.m.
ET: durable goods orders for September — consensus +0.6% month over month, prior −0.1%.

Same time: orders excluding transportation +0.6% (prior +0.3%); excluding defense 0.0% (prior +0.1%).

At 2:00 p.m.
ET: new home sales for September — 0.66 million units expected, prior 0.684 million; month-over-month change estimated −3.5%, prior +6.4%.

Also at 2:00 p.m.
ET: Conference Board consumer confidence for October — estimate 80.5, prior 81.9.

Those reads cover factory demand, new housing, and household mood before midweek Fed and earnings.

Which of the three do you watch first on Tuesday?

slots.title: Thursday 12:30: GDP, PCE, jobless claims
slots.body:
Thursday, Oct. 29, 12:30 p.m.
ET stacks growth, inflation, labor, and spending in one print.

- GDP growth rate Q3 quarter over quarter — estimate 3.2%, prior 2.2%

- Core PCE price index year over year (Sep) — estimate 3.1%, prior 3.0%

- Core PCE price index month over month (Sep) — estimate 0.3%, prior 0.2%

- PCE price index year over year (Sep) — estimate 3.6%, prior 3.4%

- Initial jobless claims (Oct. 24 week) — estimate 196K, prior 194K

- Personal spending month over month (Sep) — estimate 0.3%, prior 0.9%

Core PCE is the inflation gauge the Fed emphasizes; GDP and spending describe how fast the economy ran in Q3 and into September.

Later that day: Atlanta Fed GDPNow (Q4) at 3:00 p.m.
ET (no estimate in the feed).

Which line in that 12:30 bundle matters most for your week?
